title: SYSK’s Fall True Crime Playlist: Who Committed the 1912 Villisca Ax Murders?
summary: Josh and Chuck cover the June 9-10, 1912 Villisca, Iowa axe murders, in which eight people (including six children) were killed in the Moore house, and the investigation that followed. They describe the crime scene staging, the early suspects (state senator Frank Jones, William Blackie Mansfield, and English preacher George Kelly, who was tried twice and acquitted), and the theory that a serial killer responsible for several Midwest axe murders in 1911-1912 (Colorado Springs, Mammoth Illinois, Ellsworth Kansas, Paola Kansas, Villisca) was the culprit. They also discuss Henry Lee Moore's 1912 Columbia, Missouri murders as a likely red herring. The episode is part of a fall true crime playlist. Listener mail about a hookworm diagnosis closes the episode.

segments.title: Teaser
segments.summary: Josh introduces the episode on the 1912 Iowa axe murders as part of a playlist.

segments.title: Opening banter and pronunciation
segments.summary: The hosts banter about axe murderers and settle the pronunciation of Villisca by calling the town hall.

segments.title: Context and sources
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh discuss how the town has become associated with the murders and mention research sources including Mike Dash in Smithsonian and Ed Epperley's site.

segments.title: Setting and the Moore household
segments.summary: Describes the location of Villisca in Montgomery County and the eight people sleeping in the Moore house after a children's Day service on June 9, 1912, including the two Stillinger girls.

segments.title: The killings
segments.summary: Describes the killer entering with Joe Moore's axe, using an oil lamp, killing the parents and then the children with the flat of the axe, then bludgeoning the victims with the blade after death.

segments.title: Staging and the morning discovery
segments.summary: The killer covered mirrors and faces, left bacon and washed up, and left before dawn. Neighbor Sarah Peckham noticed no activity and Ross Moore found the bodies.

segments.title: Contaminated crime scene and search
segments.summary: Over a hundred people, including townspeople, entered the house, damaging the crime scene. Marshal Hank Horton was involved and bloodhounds searched the countryside without success.

segments.title: Suspect Frank Jones
segments.summary: State senator and businessman Frank Jones was a suspect due to a rivalry with Joe Moore over John Deere business and an alleged affair with his daughter-in-law. The Burns detective James Wilkerson suspected hired killer William Blackie Mansfield, who had an alibi.

segments.title: Suspect George Kelly
segments.summary: George Kelly, an Englishman and traveling preacher, was suspected due to his presence at the children's service and a lewd letter sent to a stenographer. He was later acquitted at trial after a hung first jury.

segments.title: Kelly trial, confession, and evidence
segments.summary: Details the alleged sexual element of Lena Stillinger's murder, the flimsy barn evidence, the retracted confession, and Kelly's return to pose as a Scotland Yard detective.

segments.title: Transition to serial killer theory
segments.summary: Summarizes that suspects were ruled out and introduces the modern serial killer theory.

segments.title: Serial killer theory and linked 1911-1912 axe murders
segments.summary: Five Midwest axe murders from October 1911 to June 1912 (Colorado Springs, Mammoth, Ellsworth, Paola, Villisca) share traits such as removed lamp chimneys, bent wicks, covered mirrors, and sexual posing. Henry Lee Moore is discussed as a likely red herring since he killed his own family in Columbia, Missouri for property.

segments.title: Further similar attacks and closing thoughts
segments.summary: Covers covered telephone, a family-targeting attack in Colorado Springs, a doorknob attempt in Villisca, and the Longmire family encounter in Paola. The hosts reflect that the killer was never caught.

segments.title: Future episode plans and resources
segments.summary: The hosts mention a future episode on Ed Gein and a recommended Smithsonian article, then plug their website and contact details.

segments.title: Listener mail: hookworm diagnosis
segments.summary: A listener from Pensacola Florida writes that his cousin's long undiagnosed symptoms matched the hookworm episode and was diagnosed with iron deficiency anemia and treated for hookworm.
